memo.title: Why practise universal competencies in childhood
paragraphs: In everyday life, children try to reach agreements, notice their feelings and finish what they started. Family tasks offer a chance to discuss these situations and possible actions.
At work, adults are assessed in four areas: how they think, handle change, work with people and pursue a result. Children have the same four universal competencies — still growing.
We have broken them into 12 everyday skills: check a story, find another option, agree on weekend plans or try again after a setback. Each can be practised with short tasks of 10–20 minutes.

abilities.title: Four universal competencies and 12 skills
abilities.subtitle: Each competency brings together three skills you can see in daily life.
abilities.literacyLead: And literacy — without it the rest does not work.
abilities.literacy: Universal literacy helps find information, judge it, tell fact from opinion — including on the internet. Subject literacy gives the child basic knowledge about safety, health and money. Example: check whether a chat message is true, or know what to do if they get lost.
abilities.ninth: Independence is not a separate item on the list. It grows when the other skills work together.
abilities.ninthNote: A child decides for themselves when they think, take others into account, and manage themselves — at the same time.

approach.title: Our approach
approach.changed: With artificial intelligence and the automation of many processes, the share of routine work is falling worldwide. Work that needs non-standard solutions, critical thinking, the art of communication and emotional intelligence is becoming central — and it needs universal competencies. The main difficulty of today’s world is uncertainty about what will be asked of our children tomorrow. So it is impossible to learn everything in advance: they will constantly have to solve unfamiliar tasks and learn again.
approach.thinking: Analyse a situation or a task, see cause and effect, offer more than one solution when there is no single right answer. Everyday example: why you do not get in a lift with a stranger, but you can with a neighbour.
approach.others: In a world where almost everything happens online, one of the key competencies is being able to communicate. Cooperate, state your view calmly, take the other person’s view into account, settle conflicts so both sides gain. Example: how to share one toy without tears.
approach.self: Understand yourself and your emotions, notice them, not act on autopilot, plan and finish even when motivation and energy have dropped. Example: not throwing the exercise book at a neighbour when something will not work.
approach.literacy: Universal literacy helps find information, judge it, tell fact from opinion — including on the internet. Subject literacy gives the child basic knowledge about safety, health and money. Example: check whether a chat message is true, or know what to do if they get lost.
approach.family: Family life offers many opportunities to practise: agreeing on weekend plans, preparing something together or discussing what you have heard. RADAR KIDS tasks help adults notice these opportunities and support their child.
approach.practice: In the tasks, the child tries an action themselves. The adult helps when needed and discusses what worked, what was difficult and what they could try next.
approach.kits: Each range has its own tasks and a focus on particular skills, shown by the catalogue tags and filter. A 24-day advent includes different tasks. A 14-day kit focuses on one skill.
approach.heroIntro: Check a story, think of another option, make an agreement, try again after a setback. These everyday actions build universal competencies.

aboutPage.title: Who makes RADAR KIDS
intro: RADAR KIDS brings together experience in corporate education and family activities. The team develops tasks that children can try with an adult and discuss afterwards.

Our development team and partners include professional methodologists, applied and clinical psychologists, lecturers and teachers, project managers, internationally certified coaches and a Candidate of Pedagogical Sciences.

In the tasks, children practise communicating, expressing opinions, thinking critically and finding their way in everyday situations. An adult supports their attempts and helps discuss the experience.

sections.title: Who processes the data
sections.text: The operator of the RADAR KIDS website. Until legal details are published, requests are handled by the founders, Julia Gordeeva and Elizabeth Sarycheva. Contacts are on the Contact page.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.text: On a kit request: name, phone or email, the child’s age, the chosen kit. On a sample request: contact details. On a company request: name, company and role, phone or email, city, date and a rough group size. We do not collect children’s names or medical data on the first form.

sections.title: Why
sections.text: To reply to the request and confirm the format. We do not send a daily newsletter without separate consent.

sections.title: How we store it
sections.text: Requests go to the operator’s email and, if a mail service is connected, to its servers. We keep them while we need to reply, then delete them on request.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.text: You can ask for a copy, a correction or deletion. Write to the contacts on this site. The consent checkbox is required: we do not send the form without it.

faq.question: How do I choose by age?
faq.answer: Start with the age filter and read who each kit is for. The safety-card edition described here is for shared activities with children aged 4–6.

faq.question: What do I need to prepare?
faq.answer: Read the contents and instructions for your chosen material. Preparation depends on the activity; there is no single list for every set.

faq.question: Can I use it with more than one child?
faq.answer: Tell the team the children’s ages and which material you are considering. Confirm usage terms and a suitable activity for that particular set.

faq.question: How can I receive a material?
faq.answer: See the selected material’s page for details on how to receive it. For questions, contact the team on Telegram; you need to send the message yourself.

faq.question: Where can I see an example?

journey.ladder: A skill is a concrete action you can notice in an ordinary day: checking a story, agreeing on weekend plans or returning to a task after a setback. Skills form universal competencies. Similar competencies are considered when assessing leadership potential at work. In the tasks, children try these actions with an adult.
journey.foundationText: These are not measured in the radar: they make the other skills possible. Safety cards are one place to start.
journey.practiceExtra: An internship consists of tasks the child tries themselves, with an adult nearby to offer support and discuss the experience.
journey.progress: The radar is not a test or diagnosis. It is a snapshot of what a child already does independently and what still needs an adult’s support. We compare the child only with themselves. Only the family sees the results.

faq.question: Who can enquire?
faq.answer: We are inviting families with children aged 7–9 to the Staying calm with change pilot. Other ages are coming soon.

faq.question: What is included?
faq.answer: Tasks at home for 14 days and a Skills Radar at the end.

faq.question: When does the pilot start and what does it cost?
faq.answer: We will reply to your enquiry with the start date and price.

faq.question: Will there be meetings or a review with a specialist?
faq.answer: These formats are not yet confirmed for the pilot. The agreed programme will be shared before it starts.

faq.question: Is this a test or diagnosis?
faq.answer: The radar is not a test or diagnosis. It is a snapshot of what a child already does independently and what still needs an adult’s support. We compare the child only with themselves. Only the family sees the results.

faq.question: Who sees the results?
faq.answer: Only the family. Companies and employers do not receive a child’s individual results.

faq.question: Do we need an internship before the cards?
faq.answer: Materials and internships are different formats. You can choose a material separately; an internship is not required before using the cards.
